hooks.text: Venus can look like a glowing halo in the sky.
Why did the dark planet Venus suddenly start glowing?
A halo of fire once surrounded a planet in transit.

title: The Secret Halo of Venus
description: Discover how a rare celestial alignment revealed the toxic atmosphere of Venus through a stunning ring of fire.

beats.text: Venus can look like a glowing halo in the sky.
beats.visual: NASA Solar Dynamics Observatory high-resolution image of the 2012 transit of Venus

beats.text: This happens when the planet passes directly in front of the Sun.
beats.visual: Diagram of the solar system showing Venus passing between Earth and the Sun

beats.text: Galileo first saw the planet change shape like our Moon in 1610.
beats.visual: Historical diagram of the phases of Venus from the 17th century

beats.text: He hid this secret in a scrambled Latin code.
beats.visual: Photograph of Galileo's original handwritten anagram for the phases of Venus

beats.text: A brilliant fire ring appeared during a rare crossing in 1761.
beats.visual: Historical illustration of the 1761 transit of Venus showing a luminous arc

beats.text: Sunlight was bending through a massive, thick atmosphere.
beats.visual: Scientific diagram of light refraction through a planetary atmosphere

beats.text: Russian scientist Mikhail Lomonosov realized another world had air.
beats.visual: Portrait of Mikhail Lomonosov, the scientist who discovered Venus's atmosphere

beats.text: That air is actually a toxic, crushing pressure cooker.
beats.visual: NASA artist concept of the dense and hazy surface of Venus

beats.text: But from Earth, it looks like a glowing halo in the sky.
beats.visual: Amateur telescopic photograph of Venus in its thin crescent phase
